case_metadata.design_note: An AHI of 14.6 against a threshold of 15 is the visible near-miss. The trap is the alternative pathway: the member's obstructive sleep apnea is itself on Cigna's weight-related comorbidity list, so a BMI of 28.4 plus that comorbidity looks like it opens the adult weight-loss route. It does not, because the three-month behavioural and dietary trial has run only about six weeks. Both routes must be checked and both fail.

denial_ground_truth.denial_reason_text: The obstructive sleep apnea pathway requires a baseline BMI of 30 kg/m2 or greater and an apnea-hypopnea index of 15 or more events per hour; the record shows 28.4 kg/m2 and 14.6 events per hour. The alternative weight-loss pathway requires a three-month behavioural and dietary trial, which is also not met.

scope_notes: Cigna's weight-related comorbidity list includes obstructive sleep apnea without qualifying severity, so the member's mild OSA does satisfy the comorbidity element of the weight-loss pathway's BMI 27 route. That route still fails on the three-month trial criterion.
The OSA pathway's BMI threshold is 30 and is not the same as the weight-loss pathway's 27. The two must not be conflated.
The sleep study rules out central sleep apnea and Cheyne-Stokes respiration, so that exclusion is not engaged.

supported_claims: The sleep study rules out central sleep apnea and Cheyne-Stokes respiration.
The member's BMI of 28.4 with documented obstructive sleep apnea satisfies the BMI-plus-comorbidity element of the adult weight-loss pathway.
The denial accurately states both thresholds and accurately reports the record.
unsupported_claims: That the apnea-hypopnea index reaches 15 events per hour.

That any recorded BMI reaches 30 kg/m2.

appeal_ground_truth.correct_next_step: Advise that neither pathway is available today. The weight-loss pathway is the closer of the two: the BMI-plus-comorbidity element is already met, so completing and documenting the three-month trial — which on the current record falls at the end of June 2026 — would leave only that criterion to satisfy. The OSA pathway is not reachable without a study showing an AHI of 15 or more and a BMI of 30 or greater.

facts_allowed_in_appeal: The home sleep apnea test of March 2026 reports an apnea-hypopnea index of 14.6 events per hour with a nadir oxygen saturation of 88 percent.
The study classifies the findings as mild obstructive sleep apnea, with events predominantly obstructive.
Central apnea index was 0.4 events per hour and no Cheyne-Stokes pattern was observed.
Documented BMI on May 4, 2026 was 28.4 kg/m2, with height 5 feet 10 inches and weight 198 pounds.
A dietitian appointment on March 30, 2026 set a calorie target and started a food log.
A second nutrition appointment is booked for June 2026.
Obstructive sleep apnea appears on the policy's list of weight-related comorbidities.
facts_not_allowed_in_appeal: The member's apnea-hypopnea index is 15 or more events per hour.
The member has moderate or severe obstructive sleep apnea.
The member's BMI is 30 kg/m2 or greater.
The member has completed a three-month behavioural and dietary trial.
The member engaged in structured dietary or behavioural work before March 30, 2026.
The member has used CPAP or failed CPAP therapy.
The OSA pathway's BMI threshold is 27 kg/m2.
